result.title: SRED: Sparse Regional Evidence Distillation Across Magnifications in Whole-Slide Imaging
result.summary: In computational pathology, high-magnification whole-slide image analysis preserves tissue detail but requires encoding many patches, whereas lower magnification reduces computation by covering a higher field of view per patch while sacrificing detail. Existing cross-magnification distillation matches features that often encode detail unreachable by low-magnification input, sometimes requiring slide-level labels that limit scalability. To address those issues, we introduce Sparse Regional Evidence Distillation (SRED), which transfers regional event occurrences that encode reachable high-level interactions between details without slide-level labels. We use a sparse autoencoder (SAE) to learn an event dictionary from 20x teacher features. Logical OR pooling records whether each event is detected in any spatially aligned patch, retaining both localized and shared evidence within the corresponding 5x region. A pretrained 5x encoder is fine-tuned to predict these regional targets without slide-level labels. Visual analysis identifies dictionary components responsive to recognizable histological patterns, supporting target interpretation. Compared with native 5x features, SRED improves average macro-F1 by 1.1 points across seven classification and grading cohorts and average C-index by 1.7 points across five survival cohorts. Runtime matches native 5x, with an average 11.58x speedup over 20x.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 SRED，用稀疏自编码器从 20x 高倍特征中学习事件字典，再以逻辑 OR 池化把空间对齐 patch 的事件存在性汇总为 5x 区域级目标，从而在无切片级标签条件下微调 5x 编码器，提升分类与生存预测并保持接近原生 5x 的运行时间。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对齐区域内的 OR 池化证据汇总 + 稀疏事件字典作为可解释监督目标」可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选、跨区域证据聚合与 latent 状态可解释性提供可核查的方法线索，但领域为病理影像，与 VLM 推理的迁移需自行判断。
